newsitem.title: ITALY: Countries must face EMU test alone - Spain's Aznar.
newsitem.headline: Countries must face EMU test alone - Spain's Aznar.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said in an interview published on Wednesday that European countries each faced an individual battle to meet tight fiscal requirements for entry to Europe's planned single currency.
Aznar was quoted as telling La Repubblica newspaper that he hoped Italy would be among the first wave of states to join European Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.

But Aznar said Italy would have to stand alone in its attempt to meet strict fiscal requirements which stipulate that countries must slash budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) before being allowed to join.
"Entry into EMU...is an individual test in which there is no room for common position-taking. We can be great friends but each of us has to pass this test by ourselves," Aznar said.
"The best thing to defend common interests is for the two countries to overcome this test on their own," he added.
"This is what I have always told (Italian Prime Minister Romano) Prodi and I am convinced that he agrees with me."
On Spain's chances of meeting EMU requirements, Aznar said a falling inflation rate made certain his country would be among the single currency's founding members.
"We will join EMU right from the start. Inflation is at 2.5 percent and could continue to fall and the peseta is stable," Aznar said.
"We are missing (the target) on the public debt requirement which is currently at 67 percent," he added. Countries must also cut public debt to 60 percent of GDP to join EMU.
"But we will make it," he said.
